title: Layout Marking in CuTe DSL
critical_patterns: Use mark_layout_dynamic() for kernels handling many sizes to avoid recompilation.
Use mark_layout_static() for fixed-size inputs to optimize performance.
Use mark_compact_shape_dynamic() when layout is fixed but dimensions vary.
constraints: Static marking requires recompilation for different sizes.
Full dynamic marking is most flexible but has slight performance overhead.
Compact dynamic marking assumes a fixed layout pattern.
compressed_summary: CuTe DSL provides layout marking to control whether a tensor's layout is treated as static or dynamic, impacting kernel specialization and performance. Static layouts are known at compile time, allowing for optimizations like loop unrolling and address calculation improvements, but require recompilation for each size. Dynamic layouts are determined at runtime, offering flexibility and reducing compilation overhead for varying sizes, but with a potential performance trade-off. The mark_layout_dynamic() function is ideal for scenarios with many input sizes, reducing the need for recompilation. Conversely, mark_layout_static() is best for fixed-size inputs where performance is critical. The mark_compact_shape_dynamic() function is a hybrid approach, maintaining a fixed layout structure while allowing dimensions to vary, optimizing performance better than full dynamic marking. Developers should explicitly mark layouts to align with their performance and flexibility needs, using dynamic marking during development for rapid iteration and static marking in production for critical paths. Profiling is recommended to determine the best approach, balancing compile-time and runtime performance. Avoid unnecessary marking if defaults suffice, and consider the impact of compilation time when choosing between static and dynamic options.
